messages:
oncall-bot: PagerDuty — HIGH: service=token-prep-prod alert: sustained CPU OOMs on token-prep replicas (>=3 pods OOMKilled across nodes). Paging oncall rotation.

alice.nguyen: seeing a flurry of OOMKilled events on token-prep, node drain symptoms on node-us-west-2a-spot-07. CPU at 98% on pods before OOM.

ben_sre: confirmed. `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep token-prep` shows 4/8 pods restartlooping, status OOMKilled. Logs show heavy prompt parsing loops.

carmen-eng-ml: probable root cause: a customer sent a malformed multi-part prompt that triggers repetitive tokenizer backtracking; earlier heuristics didn't catch it. We saw similar pattern in staging but not production.

alice.nguyen: grabbing kube logs from one OOM pod:

```
2024-09-18T20:14:02Z token-prep[1]: parsing prompt id=ab12... span=0..24 backlog=128
2024-09-18T20:14:02Z token-prep[1]: tokenize: entering nested loop on whitespace-splitting
2024-09-18T20:14:03Z token-prep[1]: memory grow: 512MB -> 1.4GB
2024-09-18T20:14:04Z kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (token-prep)
2024-09-18T20:14:04Z kubernetes: Pod oomkilled: token-prep-7dfc9d8f9-abcde
```

ben_sre: also seeing prefix cache thrash: high evictions on /var/cache/tokenizer/kv -> disk churn + CPU. That pushes GC and causes OOM.

mike-platform: checking node metrics — the nodes with OOMs are spot instances with CPU steal spikes, which amplifies CPU pressure. We have autoscaler spikes but pods keep restarting before scale completes.

joan-cs: customer-impact: support funnel shows 2 customers with 5xxs and increased latency starting ~20:14 UTC. Ticket numbers: CS-7212, CS-7213.

carmen-eng-ml: mitigation plan (short-term): 1) throttle incoming prompt size at the ingress gateway for token-prep route; 2) increase request concurrency limits for token-prep pods to avoid heavy single-thread loops; 3) roll token-prep to image with extra safety guard (max-token-scan=10000).

alice.nguyen: executing quick config change: applying a rate limit rule on envoy for /v1/tokenize: `limit_req zone=tokenize burst=5 nodelay` — pushing patch now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: patch/tokenize-rate-limit to namespace inference (canary 1/8).

ben_sre: also cordoning node-us-west-2a-spot-07 to stop new pods landing: `kubectl cordon node-us-west-2a-spot-07` — done. Will drain after we stabilize.

mike-platform: autoscaler engaged but backing off due to PodDisruptionBudgets. I'm temporarily relaxing PDB on token-prep so we can reschedule onto larger on-demand nodes.

alice.nguyen: rolled out canary rate limit, can see a small drop in error rate in the next 30s.

joan-cs: update for CS: temporary mitigation applied, engineering rolling fix. We may see reduced throughput for heavy prompts; informing customers proactively.

carmen-eng-ml: medium-term: 1) add tokenizer fast-path to avoid nested backtracking for malformed input; 2) add circuit breaker that returns 4xx for extremely long token streams; 3) add memory caps per tokenizer worker so a single prompt can't OOM the process.

ben_sre: additional observation: one node showed `kernel: oom_reaper` and then a kubelet restart; investigating if kubelet flaps caused container restarts.

alice.nguyen: ran `kubectl logs token-prep-7dfc9d8f9-abcde -n inference --previous` and captured the offending prompt shape — handing off to Carmen for deterministic regression test.

carmen-eng-ml: got it. I'll add the prompt to the eval set and run local fuzz tests. Also preparing a quick patch that short-circuits extreme recursion.

mike-platform: moved 3 token-prep replicas to on-demand nodes and set nodeAffinity to avoid spots for this deploy. CPU usage normalized on the new nodes.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: patch/tokenize-rate-limit -> 8/8 canary->prod.

alice.nguyen: errors trending down: 5xx rate from 1.9% -> 0.3% over 6 minutes. CPU usage on token-prep pods dropped from 95% to 40%.

joan-cs: letting affected customers know via CS with ETA for followup. No data exfiltration, only availability/latency impact.

ben_sre: oncall handoff: I'm going offline in 30m; handing to alice.nguyen. Actions to carry forward: watch for replays, confirm PDB relaxation restored, coordinate with Carmen on patch rollout.

alice.nguyen: acknowledged. I'll keep the channel open and escalate to Eng-Platform if we see node flaps again.

oncall-bot: Incident update recorded: incident-204321-tokenize-hotloop. Severity: SEV3 -> SEV2 (mitigated).

joan-cs: closing note: customers updated, postmortem owner assigned (carmen-eng-ml). Next: postmortem should include gating for malformed prompts, rate limit thresholds, and infra hardening to avoid spot-CPU-steal cascades.

carmen-eng-ml: taking postmortem. Will schedule follow-up with CS and Platform for remediation timeline.
